sections.title: Getting started
sections.summary: New here? The Set up guide walks you through it: copy the script's folder, plug in the controller and start Live. Live picks the script up by itself, on Windows and macOS. There is nothing to set up in Live. After that: connect the controller and start Live. The script starts the Maschine Bridge, which takes over the hardware: no Controller Editor, no MIDI mode, a real SHIFT key. While Live loads, the screen shows Waiting for Live; when the set is ready, a rainbow wave sweeps across the pads. Your note repeat rate, arp settings, chord type and voicing, drum colours and velocity curve are remembered between Live sessions.

tour.intro: Connect the controller and start Live: the Maschine Bridge takes over the hardware, with a real SHIFT key. No Controller Editor, no MIDI mode.

notes.title: Using the MASCHINE plug-in (Expansions)
notes.text: NI's MASCHINE plug-in (VST / AU) can stay in your set. While Live runs, the controller stays with Live: the plug-in doesn't take it. The pads still play the plug-in on its track, and its browser and pages work with the mouse (see MASCHINE plug-in in your Live sets). Or play the Expansions' kits without the plug-in: BROWSER > MASCHINE Kits (see BROWSER: browse and load). To control the plug-in from the hardware instead, use v1.6.1 (a separate download: reply to your purchase email) in NI's MIDI mode, where SHIFT + MASCHINE (MK3, MASCHINE+: SHIFT + CHANNEL) switches between MASCHINE and Live.

notes.title: Activate once on each computer
notes.text: Until this computer is activated, the controller shows the activation pages and Live doesn't connect. Press the encoder: the activation page opens in your browser. Your browser may ask whether this page may talk to apps on this computer: choose Allow. That lets the page reach MASCHINE for Ableton Live on this computer, and nothing else. Enter the licence key from your purchase email and the email you bought with, then Activate. Within a few seconds the controller works and Live connects. There are two editions. MIKRO MK3 covers the MIKRO MK3. MK3, MASCHINE+ & MIKRO MK3 covers all three controllers. A key works on 3 computers. Moving to another one? Deactivate this computer first: in the controller's settings choose Licence (just before About) and CONFIRM, and the licence page opens in your browser. Choose Deactivate this computer there. Once activated, it works offline too. It checks itself online now and then, and a computer that stays offline for 90 days is asked to go online once.

sections.title: Highlights
sections.summary: The best of it in a minute. Each one is explained in its own section below.

items.headline: A screen that shows what you play and turn

items.does: A chord on every pad, always in Live's key: triads to 9ths, with voicings.
Note repeat that follows pad pressure: slide the touch strip to set its rate, or touch it while holding pads to repeat them on the spot. Plus an arpeggiator, all recorded exactly on Live's grid.
items.headline: Note repeat and an arpeggiator that follow pad pressure

sections.title: PATTERN: clips
sections.summary: A 4x4 view of Live's Session clips (4 tracks x 4 scenes). Pad colours follow the clip colours; playing clips are bright, and a clip waiting to start (Live's launch quantization) blinks in its colour, red when it will record. Recording a new clip (an empty slot, or VARIATION + pad) selects its track, so Live's auto-arm arms it (the dimmed arm, which follows the track you select; tracks armed for real are disarmed), and the pads switch to the drum pads or the keyboard so you can play into it right away. With a Record length set (REC + TURN), the new clip records exactly that many bars and then loops.

The return tracks and the Master always sit on the last pads (two returns: pads 2 and 3, Master on pad 4); TURN scrolls the other tracks. Colours follow the tracks: the selected track brightest, a soloed one bright in its colour, an armed one red, a muted one (or one silenced by another's solo) dim white, a step brighter when selected, as on the drum pads.

sections.title: PAD MODE: drums
sections.summary: The 16 visible pads of the track's Drum Rack. Hitting a pad plays it and focuses it in Live (like MASCHINE focusing a sound). Pads are coloured by chain colour or by name (see the colour table); a muted pad (or one silenced by another's solo) is dim white, a step brighter when selected, as in TRACK. While a clip plays, the pads of the notes it plays light up. Hold a pad and turn for a quick edit, as in MASCHINE: TURN changes its volume (1 dB a click, SHIFT + TURN 0.1 dB), PUSH + TURN its tune in semitones (its Simpler or Drum Sampler). The pad still plays; the screen shows the pad and the value until you let go. Hold several pads to change them together, each from its own level; one hold is one undo step.
sections.swatches_note: Name colours: pads use their chain colour by default; press PAD MODE again to colour them by name instead (it is remembered). A chain without a colour also gets its name colour. The name is read word by word, first word first, as sample names start with the kind of sound (Kick BlackEarth 1, ClosedHH Dev, BD_Deep_01); a word counts when it starts with one of these words, and short abbreviations (BD, SN, HH, OH ...) only as whole words. Anything else is white.

sections.summary: The pads walk up Live's current scale (root note bright). Root and scale are Live's own, so changing them here changes Live's Scale settings and vice versa, including per-clip scales. While a clip plays, the pads of the notes it plays light up. The pads are in the track's colour (with a MIDI clip selected: the clip's) and follow it at once when you recolour it. On a track with a Drum Rack, KEYBOARD gives the drum pads.

The pads follow the track's or MIDI clip's colour, as KEYBOARD's. On a track with a Drum Rack, CHORDS gives the drum pads.

sections.title: STEP: step sequencer
sections.summary: The pads are 16 steps of the focused sound (the focused drum pad, or the last keyboard note) in the focused clip, read like text as in MASCHINE: step 1 top left (pad 13), step 16 bottom right (pad 4). The playhead runs across the pads while the clip plays, and the page follows it on longer clips (after you change the page yourself, it follows again once the playhead reaches your page). Hold a step to edit it, as in MASCHINE: the screen shows Step N and its value; TURN changes the velocity (1-127), SHIFT + TURN the length in steps, PUSH + TURN nudges the note up to 7/16 of a step earlier or later. Hold several steps to change them together; one hold is one undo step. A tap on a lit step removes it when you let go. On a Drum Rack the steps light in the selected drum pad's colour and follow when you pick another pad; on an instrument track, in the clip's colour.

sections.title: Playing: velocity, repeat, arp, touch strip
sections.summary: The bridge plays the notes itself, next to the hardware, so the pads can do things one-note-per-pad MIDI can't: chords, arpeggios, note repeat that follows pressure.

tour.intro: The bridge plays the notes itself, next to the hardware: chords, arpeggios, note repeat that follows pressure.

items.does: Hold: note repeat while held. Tap: latch on / off. From clip or scene mode it brings up the drum pads or keyboard until repeat stops. The pads flash with the notes. Repeats and arp notes follow Live's beat and land exactly on its grid when you record (Live's Record Quantization follows the rate meanwhile); 100 % gate, like MASCHINE. A hit goes to the nearest grid line: a bit early, its first note waits for the line; a bit late, it plays at once. One hit never makes two notes (the arpeggiator too).

items.does: Undo (an arrow in the screen's corner). A recording of your pads is one take, and one undo takes the whole take (a Take popup): in PAD MODE, KEYBOARD and on a locked track, whether you started it on the controller (an empty slot, VARIATION + pad, REC) or with the mouse. Live's own undo takes it in one go too (Live may list it as two steps: the clip's length and the clip). An overdub takes back only the notes you added; the clip's old notes stay. While it still records, the take goes and recording goes on.

sections.summary: MASCHINE's transport, in Live. Record length: hold REC and turn to choose Free, 1, 2, 4 or 8 bars (the screen shows it; MIKRO: also in the MASCHINE settings). A pad on an empty slot in PATTERN then records exactly that long, stops recording by itself and the clip loops; Free records until you stop it. A REC tap switches session record on its release, unless you turned meanwhile.

sections.title: Record automation
sections.summary: MASCHINE's Auto Write, in Live's Session clips. Hold AUTO and turn: what you turn is written into the playing clip of its track, as the clip's own automation, while the clip loops. Only what you turn is written. Let go and it plays back on the next loop. One hold is one undo step. Live's automation arm stays as it is. sections.title: PLUG-IN: device parameters (MIKRO)
sections.summary: The encoder controls one parameter of the selected device at a time. Parameters come in pages: Ableton's own banks for Live's devices (Filter, Envelope...), the visible macros of a rack, or groups of 8 for plug-ins. The screen shows the device, the page and how many there are (Macros 2/2; on two lines, the device after the track's box on line 1 and the count in the corner), and the parameter's name and value. A rack has as many macros as it shows in Live (click the rack's + macro button for up to 16); a hidden macro you renamed or mapped stays reachable on a last page, and showing or hiding macros updates the pages at once. Each device remembers where you were.

notes.title: Simpler
notes.text: On a Simpler the first page (Main) starts with Mode: Classic, One-Shot or Slicing (turning it switches Simpler's mode in Live). Next comes Filter Freq, or in Slicing Cursor: a position in the sample, shown as a time; PUSH on it adds a slice marker there, or removes the slice marker the cursor is on. When the cursor sits on a slice marker, its time ends with the marker's number (for example 1.00 s #4), so you know which marker PUSH removes. Then S Start and S Length in Classic. In One-Shot and Slicing they are Start and End, which move the sample's start and end markers (the ones you drag with the mouse). Filter Res (in Slicing also Filter Freq) comes first on the Filter page. Tip: with SNAP on in Simpler, Start and Length jump in big steps (Live snaps them to the sample's transients, with the mouse too). Turn SNAP off in Simpler to move them freely.

sections.title: BROWSER: browse and load (MIKRO)
sections.summary: Live's browser on the hardware screen, Recents first (the last 50 things you loaded with the browser: presets, devices, samples, MASCHINE kits and Live Sets, newest first; one loaded again moves to the top; kept when Live restarts; hidden until you load something), then Favorites (two folders: MASCHINE, the kits you starred in MASCHINE, and Mine, what you starred with SHIFT + STAR; a folder with nothing in it is hidden, and one alone is listed straight), then Live's sidebar: Collections (Live's Favorites and your coloured collections), MASCHINE Kits, MASCHINE Samples, Live Sets, the library (Sounds, Drums, Instruments ...), and the folders you added to Places. Live Sets opens at once and lists the sets in your User Library, your Places and the current project, newest first. The list keeps itself up to date: a set you deleted never shows, and a new one (a Save As into a new project folder too) appears within seconds; PUSH on one opens it at once, as a double click on the file would (Live asks to save your changes first, as usual). MASCHINE Kits (with MASCHINE Expansions or the MASCHINE library installed, from MASCHINE 2 or MASCHINE 3, Maschine Central too; any Live 12) lists your Expansions and their kits: PUSH on a kit loads it as a Drum Rack, pad for pad as in MASCHINE: onto the selected MIDI track, replacing its instrument (effects after it stay), or on a new MIDI track named after the kit (# Kit name, so Live numbers it) when an audio track is selected. Each pad is a Simpler in 1-Shot, so a hit rings out; long synth, vocal, FX, atmosphere and loop sounds play while held instead. The pads and the Drum Rack's chains get the drum colours by sound name (see PAD MODE). A drum-synth sound plays NI's recording of it where there is one; a sound that is a plug-in in MASCHINE (Massive, Monark ...) stays an empty pad with its name, to put your own sound on. Turning onto a kit plays NI's own preview of it through Live's preview (Cue output, preview switched on in Live's browser), like clicking a sample in Live's browser; the script puts the previews in your User Library (MASCHINE Kit Previews, as hard links: no extra disk space) the first time you open MASCHINE Kits, and picks up newly installed Expansions the same way. On Live 12.0 to 12.3 the kits are prepared once, in the background, the first time MASCHINE Kits opens: they are listed at once, with a Preparing kits 42% row on top that counts up and goes by itself (after a Live restart it carries on where it stopped). A kit you push before it is ready is prepared first and loads by itself in a moment. You'll also see the kits in Live's browser, under User Library > MASCHINE Kit Presets. Your MASCHINE favourites come along, in a one-way sync: the kits you star in MASCHINE show with a ★ in Favorites and in MASCHINE Kits' own Favorites folder, next to the ones you starred on the controller (a kit starred in both is listed once). Star or unstar kits in MASCHINE and the lists follow, also while Live runs (the next time the list opens). The controller only reads MASCHINE's favourites and never changes them: a kit starred in MASCHINE stays starred here (the screen says Still starred / in MASCHINE; star / unstar it in MASCHINE). Expansions you add or remove are followed: a removed Expansion's kits leave the lists, and a new one's favourites appear once MASCHINE has scanned it. Favorites lists are sorted by name, as in MASCHINE. MASCHINE Samples (Live 12.4 and later) lists MASCHINE's sample types: Kick, Snare, Clap, Hihat and the rest. Open a type to see every sample of it from all your MASCHINE libraries and Expansions, by name, each with its library's cover. PUSH loads the sample into a Simpler: the selected Simpler, the track's, or the selected drum pad's. On an empty MIDI track or an empty drum pad a Simpler is added first, and one undo removes the Simpler and the sample together. The first time it opens it may say Loading... for a moment, then the types fill in by themselves. This is the way to play the Expansions in Live without the MASCHINE plug-in, which takes the controller away from the script (see Getting started).

items.does: On a Drum Synth: its card. DS Kick, DS Snare, DS HH, DS Cymbal, DS Tom, DS Clap, DS Clang, DS FM and DS Sampler each have their own drawing and icon.
items.headline: Each Drum Synth on a card of its own, with a drawing and an icon

items.does: Hit the pad: its Drum Synth's drawing plays the hit, as loud as you played it. Another pad focuses its own synth.
Turn a knob: the drawing and its decay line follow the sound.

sections.title: MASCHINE Kits (MK3)
sections.summary: Play your MASCHINE Expansions in Live without the MASCHINE plug-in. BROWSER > MASCHINE Kits lists your Expansions and their kits. A turn onto a kit plays its preview, and a load makes it a Drum Rack, pad for pad as in MASCHINE. Your MASCHINE favourites come along, starred.

tour.intro: Your MASCHINE Expansions in Live, no plug-in: browse, hear, load a kit as a Drum Rack.

items.does: Open the browser. Knob 1 (or a turn on the top list): MASCHINE Kits.
items.headline: Open MASCHINE Kits in the browser

items.does: Open an Expansion: its kits on the right screen.
Turn onto a kit: its preview plays.
Load the kit as a Drum Rack on the selected track. The browser closes and the pads light in the kit's colours.
items.headline: Load a kit as a Drum Rack, the pads in its colours

sections.title: Section page (MK3)
sections.summary: SHIFT + SCENE opens MASCHINE's Section page on Live's Arrangement. The left screen shows the song: the sections between Live's locators, the tracks' clips as lanes, the playhead. The right screen shows the locators as tiles, the playing one white. The pads are the first 16 locators: the hint line says 'Pads: jump to a locator'.

tour.intro: Live's Arrangement as MASCHINE's Section page: the song on the screens, the locators on the pads.

items.does: The Section page on / off (hold SCENE: only while held; let go and the page you were on comes back, PLUG-IN too).
items.headline: SHIFT + SCENE: the Section page

items.does: Jump to that locator (Live's jump: on the beat while it plays). The pads are the locators in the selected track's colour, the playing one white, the picked one bright.
items.headline: Your song's locators on the pads: jump on the beat

items.does: The SHIFT functions, as in every mode (undo, redo, quantize, copy ...). Plain pads stay the locators.
Tilt the 4-D left / right to pick the previous / next locator (framed white). Push: jump to it.
items.headline: Tilt the 4-D: the previous / next locator

sections.title: BROWSER: MASCHINE's browser (MK3)
sections.summary: With the screens, BROWSER is MASCHINE's browser on Live's browser: the left screen shows where you are (the category and its folders as tiles), the right one the results. The same lists as on the MIKRO (see BROWSER: browse and load): Favorites, Live's sidebar, MASCHINE Kits, MASCHINE Samples, Live Sets, the library and your Places. Turning onto a MASCHINE kit plays its preview, and a load closes the browser, back to the page you came from.

tour.intro: Live's browser on the two screens, as MASCHINE's: categories, folders and results, with MASCHINE Kits and your favourites.

items.does: Browser on / off (it opens where you left it).
Scroll the results (tilt the 4-D up / down too).
Open the folder, or load the item onto the selected track (tilt the 4-D right too; left: back up one level).
items.headline: Open a folder or load the item

items.does: The category: Favorites, Live Sets, Sounds, Drums, Instruments ...
items.headline: Knob 1: the category

items.does: Knobs 2-4 in Live's tagged categories (Sounds, Drums, Instruments, effects ...): TYPE, SUBTYPE and CHARACTER, as MASCHINE's tag filters. Touch or turn one: its tags pop up as a cloud. Elsewhere the knobs are the folder levels.
items.headline: Browse by Live's tags on the knobs, as MASCHINE's tag filters

items.does: PREVIOUS / NEXT load the previous / next result (only the one you stop on goes into Recents), ★ shows Favorites (SHIFT: star / unstar the result), LOAD loads it.
items.headline: PREVIOUS, NEXT, Favorites and LOAD on the display buttons

items.does: Hot-Swap the selected device (PLUG-IN's button 8 too). The browser opens as your last swap of that device left it: the same filters on, the loaded result highlighted, nothing playing until you turn. A load replaces the device. SHIFT + BROWSER again cancels.
items.headline: Hot-Swap the selected device, where your last swap left it

items.does: In a Hot-Swap: CANCEL. Nothing loads, and the browser closes, back to the page you came from. In plain browsing it is empty. SHIFT + LOAD: PREHEAR on / off. A result plays only when you scroll onto it.
items.headline: CANCEL a Hot-Swap, PREHEAR on / off

items.does: Knob 4 CHARACTER (SHIFT: GENRE). Knob 7 sorts Live Sets by name or newest first.
items.headline: Genre, and Live Sets sorted by name or date

items.does: The page you were on comes back.
items.headline: Close or load: back to the page you were on

changes.v1: Controller Editor template, MIDI mode (SHIFT + MASCHINE), choose ports in Live
changes.v2: Copy the script into the User Library, plug in the controller and start Live. Live picks the script up by itself on Windows and macOS, and the bridge starts with Live. Nothing to set up in Live
The real SHIFT button; RESTART restarts playback

changes.what: Tracks, scenes and steps on the pads
changes.v2: Read like text from pad 13 (A), as printed and as in MASCHINE; return tracks and Master stay on the last pads
Start / stop like MASCHINE; SHIFT + PLAY continues where it stopped; RESTART plays from the start

changes.v1: Deleted the focused clip / track / scene
changes.v2: Does nothing (safety); SHIFT + ERASE deletes the focused item
SHIFT + BROWSER

changes.v1: BROWSER: Live's browser view; STAR: nothing
changes.v2: BROWSER: the browser on the controller's screen; STAR: your favourites; SHIFT + STAR stars any item
Tap NOTE REPEAT (SHIFT + NOTE REPEAT now switches to the arpeggiator)
SHIFT + FIXED VEL, as in v1 (the selected notes, else every note)
Step undo / step redo: the take's last note or chord, one at a time, as in MASCHINE
Fixed velocity on / off
SHIFT + ◀ ▶ (CHORDS and STEP are now chord and step modes)
SHIFT + PLUG-IN (PLUG-IN now controls device parameters)
Tap GROUP (hold: temporary)
DUPLICATE + unlit pad (SHIFT + pads are the edit functions in every mode, TRACK included)

Chords, arpeggiator, step sequencer, hardware browser (Live Sets open from it too), MASCHINE Expansion kits as Drum Racks (MIKRO), parameter control, Simpler's mode, sample markers and slices, pitch / mod strip, record variations (VARIATION + pad), take undo and step undo / redo, MASCHINE Samples (every MASCHINE sample by type), an empty Simpler from SAMPLING, the MK3's CHANNEL page and PERFORM strip,clip progress and parameter value on the strip (touch to jump / set), a silent metronome on the strip while recording, fixed-length recording (REC + TURN), quick edits on a held step or drum pad, humanize, screen feedback, a screen saver, light brightness and a start mode (MIKRO settings), pads light instantly when played
The drum pads (the keyboard without a Drum Rack); MIKRO: choose Pads, Pattern, Scene, Step or Track in the settings
Free as before, or exactly 1, 2, 4 or 8 bars, then it loops (REC + TURN)

changes.v1: NI's MIDI mode: SHIFT + MASCHINE (MK3, MASCHINE+: SHIFT + CHANNEL) switches between MASCHINE and the script
changes.v2: The plug-in stays in the set and the controller stays with Live: the pads play the plug-in, its browser and pages work with the mouse (or use v1.6.1 to switch on the fly)

MASCHINE's pages for Live on both screens (mixer, devices as pictures, browser, Section page ...). Nothing to switch: on Windows NI's software draws them, on macOS they switch to Live by themselves the first time

Recents at the top of BROWSER: the last 50 things you loaded with it, newest first, kept when Live restarts. Favorites has two folders: MASCHINE (the kits you starred in MASCHINE) and Mine (your stars on the controller)
On the controller: MIKRO MASCHINE (a list), MK3 SETTINGS (four tabs on the knobs). A switch that changes something outside Live asks first: CANCEL or CONFIRM
